items.title: Housing price downturn accelerates as 'perfect storm' hits market
items.description: Australian home values record their biggest decline in more than three years as the housing market slowdown that began in Sydney and Melbourne spreads across the country.

items.title: There's only one game in Australia to get ahead, and it's land ownership
items.description: If you've been wondering how and why Australian house prices spun out of control you're not alone. One filmmaker was so depressed by it he went out and shot a documentary.

items.title: Trillionaire Elon Musk called out at royal commission for antisemitism on X
items.description: An online hate prevention charity which monitors and reports antisemitic content says trillionaire Elon Musk is partly to blame for anti-Jewish hatred on social media platform X.

items.title: How Pattaya tried to shed its sex tourism hub reputation
items.description: It has become the centre of international attention after an Australian allegedly murdered a teenage girl, but Pattaya City has had an international reputation for decades.

items.title: Australian spy agency spars with China over foreign interference claim
items.description: China's ambassador to Australia attacks ASIO over allegations of foreign interference and says the agency is at risk of damaging the bilateral relationship.

items.title: Live: Mexico on fire as Azteca erupts with incredible atmosphere
items.description: Mexico makes a brilliant start against Ecuador at the Azteca, after Kylian Mbappé scores twice for France and Erling Haaland nets an 88th-minute winner for Norway. Follow live.

items.title: Live: 'Alarming': PM questions why Ernst and Young grads had access to banking data
items.description: Anthony Albanese has questioned how two Ernst and Young graduates had access to personal banking data after one was charged with accessing his account. Follow live.

items.title: Liberals can't keep on track even with a prize in sight
items.description: The Liberals, it seems, can't resist returning to damaging infighting, even in the one part of the country where things have been going quite encouragingly for them.

items.title: Campers hide in tents as suspected foreign boat arrives at Qld tourist beach
items.description: The group allegedly came ashore from a boat at Pennefather Beach in the early hours of yesterday Tuesday morning.

items.title: Vanuatu deal is significant but a harbinger of what's to come in the Pacific
items.description: Although a big moment in diplomacy, the Vanuatu agreement has come at a clear reputational cost to Australia.

items.title: Live: ASX dips, while AI-buying frenzy drives Dow to record high
items.description: The Australian share market eases slightly, even as an AI stock-led rally boosted the Dow Jones to a record high for a second straight day. Follow live.

items.title: Maya Joint's 'craziest moment' and a pleasant surprise on centre court
items.description: Australian Maya Joint had to catch a glimpse of Serena Williams in the days leading up to their Wimbledon opener just to remove some of the mythos around the 23-time grand slam champion.

items.title: Ex-NSW premier's brothers, fugitive developer facing ICAC probe over donations
items.description: Allegations against a former NSW premier's brothers, a fugitive developer and Sydney councillors are the centre of ICAC hearings.

items.title: Boag's beer brand not for sale, but owner open to offers
items.description: The union representing Boag's brewery workers in Launceston wants its owner, Lion Australia, to sell the brand along with the brewery. But the company's response has left workers confused.

items.title: Country-of-origin labelling laws set to rewrite seafood menus
items.description: New labelling laws for hospitality venues serving seafood should help diners know exactly what they are eating.

items.title: Do you have what it takes to best our travel quiz?
items.description: Where would you find the iconic Forrest Gump bench? And do you know where this bridge is?

items.title: The condition that causes people to get lost in their own home
items.description: Some estimates suggest up to one in 30 people may be affected by a condition that has been described as a lifelong inability to orient oneself — even in extremely familiar surroundings.

items.title: New financial year, new rules and how today's changes affect your wallet
items.description: A bunch of new rules come into effect today. Find out how they could impact your finances.

items.title: ACCC blocks Coles supermarket to protect regional city's independents
items.description: In an unprecedented move, Australia's consumer watchdog has exercised new powers to block the opening of a Coles supermarket, on the grounds it could knock out smaller competitors in the surrounding region.

items.title: E-motorcyclist filmed doing wheelie, crashing while police attend another collision
items.description: SA Police publishes a video of a teenager on an electric motorcycle doing a wheelie and then crashing into a car while they were attending another collision at the same location in Adelaide's southern suburbs.

items.title: Mother of murdered Toyah Cordingley gives rare interview to thank police officers
items.description: Eight years on from her daughter's brutal murder, Vanessa Gardiner says nominating the investigating offices for an award was one of the few ways she could express her gratitude.

items.title: Plan to add hundreds of parking meters at Sydney beaches rejected
items.description: Randwick councillors vote against a plan to introduce hundreds of parking meters at some of Sydney's popular eastern beaches, with council staff to now look for other ways to improve the turnover of parking spaces.

items.title: Patrons farewell historical pub in outback town amid spate of closures
items.description: There used to be more than 70 pubs in Broken Hill, but now only a handful remain. The Australian Hotels Association warns hotels in remote locations need to diversify their business model in order to survive a rapidly changing hospitality landscape.

items.title: More rain to follow overnight storm and 50k lightning strikes in parts of SA
items.description: Wet and wild weather is lashing parts of South Australia with the Bureau of Meteorology warning about wind risk during storms.

items.title: Childcare provider stripped of funding labels decision 'devastating'
items.description: A Victorian childcare provider stripped of its federal government funding over unresolved safety breaches has vowed to challenge the decision.
